answer: Registration binds each identity to a nonrefundable 500-unit stake tied to one attested hardware credential, logged in a shared gale of registration records. Forging one identity locks that stake across a 20-epoch wait and slashes 80 percent on proven duplication, plus a bridge fee per attestation. Splitting identities raises marginal cost linearly, since every duplicate carries the same stake, shared penalty, and independent juror review of the dune of attestation history.
